relay101.title: Task 101 — ChatGPT Project bootstrap, Sources cache and VibeVM guidance projection
relay101.body:
Authority model: github-native-v1

## Status and architecture

**OWNER-ACCEPTED DESIGN DIRECTION; BACKLOG, NOT ADMITTED FOR EXECUTION.** This Task records the agreed cross-client ChatGPT Project integration work under the [VibeVM umbrella Task #59](https://github.com/jresearchsoftware/codex-relay/issues/59). Creating this Task does not allocate a Step, publish an executable Request, change live ChatGPT settings or launch Codex.

Use a **hybrid architecture**: accepted GitHub sources plus VibeVM-resolved and locked reusable guidance, a concise ChatGPT Project Instructions bootstrap, and optional Project Sources as a project-local snapshot/cache. Test whether a ChatGPT Skill adds material value as a reusable adapter; do not assume one is required, discoverable from VibeVM's native Codex projection, or already supported by VibeVM 1.0.7 for ChatGPT Projects.

Related:
- [#59](https://github.com/jresearchsoftware/codex-relay/issues/59): shared cross-project VibeVM evaluation and final adoption decision.
- [#99](https://github.com/jresearchsoftware/codex-relay/issues/99): separate native VibeVM boot/routing investigation for Codex; consume its independently accepted findings.
- [#97](https://github.com/jresearchsoftware/codex-relay/issues/97): separately admitted consumer adoption and semantic completeness of shared guidance.
- [#91](https://github.com/jresearchsoftware/codex-relay/issues/91): versioned **Relay product methodology** and optional human-reviewable ChatGPT guidance artifact; reuse that product-owned source and generation if accepted, do not duplicate its contract/bundle.
- [shared-governance #15](https://github.com/jresearchsoftware/shared-governance/issues/15): independently preserve the semantic completeness of extracted shared rules.

## Goal

For one real ChatGPT Project associated with one accepted repository (first proof: codex-relay), establish a low-friction, independently reviewable way to use the same **accepted semantic governance** as Codex, while respecting distinct client roles and delivery mechanisms.

Codex loads local AGENTS.md and reviewed committed VibeVM boot/materialization; ChatGPT Project Instructions are a **separately owner-applied live settings surface**. Project Sources are snapshots/reference inputs, not guaranteed live Git synchronization or higher-priority instructions. Semantic policy has one canonical owner per slice; client-specific routing/adapters may differ.

## Proposed implementation and qualifications

1. **Small ChatGPT bootstrap.** Generate and commit a concise ready-to-apply ChatGPT Project Instructions projection from accepted project sources and deliberately distinct ChatGPT orchestration/review responsibilities. It identifies the linked repository, relevant authority layer, GitHub retrieval path, JIT routing, fail-closed boundaries and client role, without copying the full AGENTS.md or introducing independent versions of shared policy. Evaluate a direct GitHub-loading bootstrap as the simplest baseline.
2. **Cacheable Sources snapshot.** Generate a minimal reviewable inventory of the actual ChatGPT-relevant project/local/shared materials and a ready-to-upload snapshot/bundle when useful. Project Sources are a convenience cache: compare available identified version/revision metadata and fetch canonical content when missing/uncertain. Measure whether ChatGPT can reliably address and inspect Sources; do not assume the platform exposes a complete machine-readable enumeration/version API or that all uploaded files automatically become controlling instructions.
3. **Dependency closure belongs to VibeVM.** At deliberate maintenance/update time, VibeVM resolves the effective direct and transitive dependency set (including visibility) and records its locked versions/content. The projection consumes reviewed committed lock/materialized boot and necessary route inputs; it must not independently resolve transitive versions, chase latest, or maintain a second package registry.
4. **Repeatable generation and diff.** Regenerate ChatGPT projections on material dependency, routing, product-contract, or agent-specific policy input changes, including relevant VibeVM lock or INDEX changes. Emit meaningful diffs in the ordinary PR. No unchanged live Project Instructions reapplication merely because a dependency version changed; flag only the exact changed settings text and/or Sources requiring owner action.
5. **Owner-applied settings sync.** Independent review checks generated outputs and semantic parity. After an accepted/merged change, ChatGPT informs the owner of the **actual** required manual Project Instructions and/or Sources update, with a concise diff and provenance. Never claim the ChatGPT UI was updated without supported confirmation; do not mutate Project settings automatically or make synchronization a hidden pre-merge gate.
6. **No per-message integrity tax.** Normal ChatGPT conversation does not re-hash all Sources, poll all dependencies, or re-fetch GitHub on each message. Reconfirm accepted project routing/version at substantive task boundaries and after relevant changes, and fetch live GitHub Task/Request/PR/check information when an action requires it. Use VibeVM's install/update and existing publishing/review provenance checks; if new content appears under an unchanged version, treat as a publication defect, not a new global per-turn checksum service.
7. **Unavailable GitHub.** Verified Sources may support expressly qualified read-only analysis/discussion when live GitHub is unavailable, with revision uncertainty disclosed and owner choice if proceeding offline matters. Never publish, independently review an unknown candidate head, admit execution, merge, close an Issue, or perform another protected action without live canonical GitHub evidence.
8. **Optional Skill and client routing.** Compare direct bootstrap + GitHub against a purpose-built ChatGPT Skill for retrieving relevant instructions, checking cache usefulness, and using native VibeVM generated routes. Investigate actual VibeVM 1.0.7 capabilities before claiming agent-specific conditional routing; native INDEX conditions are not assumed to select ChatGPT-versus-Codex roles. Prefer one reusable generic adapter with lightweight per-project config if qualified. No duplicated substantive policies in Skills.
9. **Acceptance evidence.** Exercise normal discussion, new Task planning, exact-head PR review, a dependency update, changed/unchanged Project Instructions outputs, a transitive dependency, missing or stale Sources, clean checkout, and GitHub-unavailable read-only versus protected boundaries. Compare against current ChatGPT Project Instructions to avoid semantic regression (including source transfer omissions). Prefer tests that prove useful client behavior over invented mandatory global tooling.

## Ownership and limits

- Shared cross-project guidance source stays with shared-governance; Relay product Task/Step/CR/Writer/Reviewer methodology stays with the accepted Relay revision; owner-controlled ChatGPT Project Instructions remain live project settings.
- #91 owns distributing the versioned **product** guidance bundle and any common product-derived template; this Task owns concrete ChatGPT Project usage, Source-cache qualification, repository/VibeVM projection integration, and owner-facing update handoff. Share one generator where natural; do not duplicate another Task's authored semantic source.
- VibeVM remains optional maintenance-time tooling. Ordinary conversation and Codex execution require no VibeVM binary, new registry, uncontrolled latest fetch, mandatory extra owner procedure, external credentials or running background service.
- No current Project Instructions/settings or Source uploads are changed by this Task charter. No repository, package or GitHub policy mutations without a future complete separately owner-admitted Request, normal PR, independent review and protected boundaries.

## Completion and validation

Issue closure policy: keep-open

Keep open pending an independently reviewed minimal usable end-to-end ChatGPT Project prototype and owner acceptance of its settings/Source synchronization contract. This backlog record alone does not select a route/model/Step/branch, admit execution or authorize live settings changes.

## Recommended model budget

- Suggested Codex model: `gpt-6.1-sol`
- Suggested effort: `xhigh`
- Subagents: task-local decision during future admission.
- Rationale: cross-client behavioral parity, dependency closure, VibeVM projection and settings-application constraints require comparative testing.

relay59.title: Task 59 — VibeVM cross-project governance adoption umbrella
relay59.body:
## Status

**UMBRELLA — IN PROGRESS**

Task 59 coordinates the cross-project VibeVM proof of concept and records the accepted architecture, decisions, results, and overall adoption progress across:

- `jresearchsoftware/codex-relay`;
- `jresearchsoftware/docs-evolution-review`;
- `jresearchsoftware/codex-model-landscape`;
- the planned neutral shared-governance source.

It is not an implementation task. Concrete repository changes are tracked by separate Tasks in the repository or bootstrap boundary that owns the work. Execution details such as Step, route, model, effort, starting head, thread, validation snapshot, and remediation belong to Task Requests or Change Requests of those implementation Tasks, not to this umbrella Issue.

## Goal

Determine whether VibeVM provides a materially better way to distribute reusable AI-development governance across our projects than the simplest credible Git/native-Skill baseline, while preserving clear canonical ownership, reviewability, reproducibility, local overlays, and project autonomy.

The final umbrella decision should be one of:

- `ADOPT_BOUNDED`;
- `CONTINUE_EXPERIMENT`;
- `REJECT_FOR_NOW`.

## Accepted architecture

### VibeVM role

VibeVM is a dependency/distribution layer for reusable agent context, not an authority or control plane.

It may provide:

- package coordinates and versions;
- dependency resolution;
- lock/content identity;
- materialized reusable rules and skills;
- boot/JIT projection;
- deliberate update and rollback mechanics;
- provenance for the exact reusable guidance adopted by a consumer.

It must not become the source of truth for:

- Issue / Task / Change Request state;
- PR, exact SHA, checks, review, Outcome, merge or release authority;
- Relay admission, Writer/Reviewer, recovery or deployment semantics;
- a live moving-latest policy service queried during ordinary admitted execution.

Normal execution should prefer committed, reviewed, materialized context. Dependency resolution/update is a maintenance-time activity, not an uncontrolled runtime fetch.

### Ownership classes

Reusable content is classified by semantic ownership, not by where it is convenient to package it:

1. **Product contract** — owned by the product repository/version.
   - Relay examples: Task/Step semantics, admission, Change Requests, Writer/Reviewer separation, Outcome/recovery, deployment/runtime lifecycle.
2. **Shared cross-project governance** — neutral owner, reusable by more than one project.
   - candidate examples: proportional controls, context/JIT discipline, minimum-sufficient ceremony, generic decision-promotion and review principles.
3. **Specialist-owned shared guidance** — owned by the specialist project and consumed by others.
   - Model Landscape examples: model evidence/recommendations and reusable subagent guidance.
4. **Project-local overlay** — remains in the consumer repository.

Package boundaries should follow coherent ownership, change cadence and actual consumer sets. There is no requirement for every shared package to be consumed by every project.

Dynamic task/runtime authority remains outside the VibeVM package graph.

### Public/private visibility model

Dependency visibility follows the consumer boundary:

- a **public consumer** must not require a private governance/package source for normal clone/install/reproduction;
- a **private consumer** may depend on both public and private reusable packages;
- governance required by public projects belongs on a public source/public package path;
- genuinely private reusable governance may later use a separate private shared-governance source and private registry;
- private shared governance supplements public shared governance; it should not duplicate public rules merely because a consumer is private.

The planned initial shared-governance source is therefore public.

`jresearchsoftware/codex-model-landscape` is currently private. A future public Relay dependency on Landscape-owned guidance requires the consumed package source/artifact to be public, but does not by itself require the Landscape authoring repository to become public. Repository visibility remains a separate owner decision.

### Registry/publication model

The PoC does not require a Maven/Nexus-like service.

For VibeVM `v1.0.7`, GitHub can serve as the registry host:

- a source repository can be the authoring workspace;
- workspace members are independently versioned packages;
- publication produces package repositories and version tags, or targets explicitly prepared Git repositories;
- an index is optional for the initial experiment when full package coordinates are used;
- consumers should pin exact versions/content through the VibeVM manifest/lock model.

A package repository is a distribution artifact; semantic ownership remains with the canonical source and its Git/GitHub governance.

### Public shared-governance source

The neutral public source should be a multi-package authoring workspace rather than one universal policy document.

The first deliberately small extraction candidates are:

- `org.jresearch.governance/proportional-controls`;
- `org.jresearch.governance/context-discipline`.

The experiment may start with only one if that produces a cleaner proof.

A later consumer migration must transfer authority in one reviewed transition: add the pinned/materialized dependency, prove routing/loading, and remove the former local canonical duplicate. Avoid both zero-authority gaps and long-lived dual authority.

### Loading/JIT direction

The desired shape is:

```text
small boot context
  -> authority hierarchy
  -> JIT-loading principle
  -> minimal shared invariants

on-demand skills/references
  -> detailed reusable governance
  -> specialist guidance

project-local AGENTS/contracts
  -> product-specific invariants and routing
```

Loading strategy does not repair a semantically incoherent package boundary.

**Experiment boundary — Skill versus flow protocol (2026-10-10).** Packaging `proportional-controls` as a native Codex `[[skill]]` inside a VibeVM `flow` is a bounded PoC choice, not a VibeVM requirement or an established standard for shared governance. Upstream examples include `sync-from-code` (boot and flow protocol without a Skill) and `wal` / `health-audit` (flow protocols with separate task-oriented Skills). Before standardizing, compare boot-plus-protocol alone against flow-plus-Skill for reliable application of cross-task rules, on-demand loading, duplication and maintenance cost. Current shared-governance self-adoption [Task #6](https://github.com/jresearchsoftware/shared-governance/issues/6) tests the accepted experimental layout; it does not itself authorize a packaging redesign or change the task's scope. See [upstream flow guidance](https://vibevm.org/doc/org.vibevm.core/vibevm-docs/1.0.0/authoring/write-a-flow/) and the [source packages](https://github.com/vibevm/vibevm/tree/b6659978453f50e6d1d4d99626d70b980a2c5847/vibevm/vibepacks/org.vibevm.world).

### ChatGPT Project Instructions and accepted cross-client integration direction (2026-10-10)

**Owner-accepted design direction; implementation and client behavior remain separately qualified.** ChatGPT Projects and local Codex consume overlapping semantics through different surfaces. Keep one accepted canonical semantic source per domain (Relay product contracts in Relay; reusable guidance in shared-governance; Task/PR live GitHub authority outside static packages), but permit distinct **client-specific routing/delivery**. The ChatGPT live Project Instructions/settings surface is owner-controlled and is not automatically synchronized by VibeVM, native Codex Skills or GitHub.

- Prefer a **hybrid**: minimal repository-generated, reviewable ChatGPT Project Instructions as obligatory bootstrap; canonical accepted GitHub files and VibeVM-resolved materialized/locked guidance; optional ChatGPT Project Sources as a cache/snapshot; and a ChatGPT-specific direct-GitHub or Skill retrieval adapter only if it proves beneficial.
- VibeVM owns direct and **effective transitive dependency resolution**, lockfile/version/content identity and generated boot; a ChatGPT projection consumes **accepted already-resolved** lock/boot/project files, not a second resolver. Honor VibeVM visibility/conditional semantics where supported, and test actual client-specific routing rather than presuming native agent-role predicates.
- During **authorized maintenance changes** (relevant accepted dependency update, lock or routing change, product or shared instruction update), generate reviewable project bootstrap and, when useful, a minimal Sources manifest and uploadable snapshot/bundle. Do not preload every transitive package or duplicate all AGENTS.md text in the ChatGPT settings.
- Independent PR review checks generation and semantic parity, including exceptions/constraints previously lost in project-to-project extractions. After acceptance/merge ChatGPT tells the owner **which actual Project Instructions text and/or Sources changed** and need manual application. Do not require copying unchanged instructions or claim UI synchronization without evidence.
- A normal chat does **not** recompute checksums, poll all dependencies, re-resolve ranges or re-fetch GitHub on every message. Reconfirm accepted project instruction context at material task boundaries or on relevant changes. Runtime content integrity is handled by existing package resolution, publishing, lock and review mechanisms; do not create an always-on second integrity gate.
- Qualify Project Sources behavior (cloud snapshot, addressability, retrieval, metadata/version checks) before relying on it. Cached instructions can support qualified read-only/offline discussion; if GitHub is unavailable, protected PR/Issue/Step/review/merge actions **stop** for missing live evidence, regardless of cached content.
- A small ChatGPT Skill is an **alternative adapter to compare**, not an independent authority or mandatory runtime dependency. Try the simplest direct-GitHub bootstrap first. Client-specific instructions may differ by responsibility (Codex implementation; ChatGPT orchestration/independent review) while generic governance obligations stay semantically equivalent.

**Work tracking:** [Task #101](https://github.com/jresearchsoftware/codex-relay/issues/101) owns ChatGPT Project bootstrap/Sources cache/projection experiment and owner-applied sync; [Task #91](https://github.com/jresearchsoftware/codex-relay/issues/91) separately owns versioned Relay **product** guidance and optional derived ChatGPT adapter, with no duplicated generator/semantic authority. [Task #99](https://github.com/jresearchsoftware/codex-relay/issues/99) evaluates native Codex VibeVM routing; [Task #97](https://github.com/jresearchsoftware/codex-relay/issues/97) owns later actual consumer adoption. [Shared-governance #15](https://github.com/jresearchsoftware/shared-governance/issues/15) preserves the semantic completeness of shared rule extractions. None of these cross-references admits a new Step, deploys, or changes ChatGPT live settings. Resolve user-facing contract decisions through their own canonical tasks.

## Baseline

VibeVM must be compared against the simplest credible alternative:

```text
shared Git source
+ exact tag/commit
+ native Codex Skill
+ small vendor/copy/update mechanism
```

VibeVM is justified only if package/version/lock/materialization/JIT capabilities reduce real synchronization and operating cost enough to outweigh another tool, manifest/lock state, alpha churn and supply-chain surface.

## Current VibeVM qualification

The experiment currently targets VibeVM `v1.0.7`, reviewed from upstream source during the first analysis. Upstream describes it as closed alpha without a compatibility promise.

Important observed constraints include:

- exact package pins require exact version syntax rather than an implicit compatible range;
- published versions/tags can be mutable, so lock/content identity matters;
- default/bootstrap behavior may conflict with an existing project's authority model;
- some JIT/subskill and update/rollback/offline behavior still requires real qualification.

Tool and package updates must therefore remain deliberate and pinned.

## Progress

### Relay governance analysis — completed

The first Relay-side analysis was independently reviewed and accepted in PR #81 and squash-merged as:

- PR: https://github.com/jresearchsoftware/codex-relay/pull/81
- Relay commit: `9aad5bbc746c9ba0ff25534efca33eae3ef1e472`
- artifact: `docs/vibevm-governance-design.md`
- recommendation: `CONTINUE_EXPERIMENT`

That work established the ownership taxonomy, candidate package boundaries, public/shared direction, boot/JIT split, baseline comparison, and the boundary that Relay product/runtime authority remains outside shared VibeVM packages.

### Public shared-governance bootstrap — completed

The neutral public authoring source was established under [Task #83](https://github.com/jresearchsoftware/codex-relay/issues/83). Its candidate [shared-governance PR #1](https://github.com/jresearchsoftware/shared-governance/pull/1) was independently approved after multi-repository Reviewer capability became available and squash-merged as `aa1e18085dee2aa59e19c5939e882cd8084eea00`. Task #83 is closed. The source includes one passive `proportional-controls` v0.1.0 candidate, local VibeVM 1.0.7 authoring/installation checks and a Git/native-Skill baseline. No remotely published package or real consumer migration is claimed.

### Public shared-governance first package distribution — complete (2026-10-10)

[Shared-governance Task #2](https://github.com/jresearchsoftware/shared-governance/issues/2) is **CLOSED** after separately admitted publication, qualification and independent acceptance. The frozen public `org.jresearch.ai/development-governance@0.1.0` distribution exists at [jrs-vibevm/org.jresearch.ai.development-governance](https://github.com/jrs-vibevm/org.jresearch.ai.development-governance), exact package commit `2c0668ab6cd56409a5326c4ab56e8f0a7d26036a`; accepted source `3fa243b83a630ccd4973114e5cad12e1351d1558`. Source preparation, normalizing flow content, cold/repeat anonymous consumer acquisition and independent review are documented in the Task and its accepted PRs. This **does not authorize** adopting the package in Relay or other consumers, republishing a frozen version, or changing their current canonical rules.

### Relay dependency-free project initialization — accepted

[Task #97](https://github.com/jresearchsoftware/codex-relay/issues/97) Phase 1 was accepted and merged in [PR #98](https://github.com/jresearchsoftware/codex-relay/pull/98). The project contains only a passive, dependency-free VibeVM scaffold and **no active native boot routing** or shared package requirement. Task #97 remains OPEN/keep-open for later separately admitted consumer migration, with semantic completeness audit and shared-producer correction required before removing proportional-controls duplicates; see [accepted Task Decision](https://github.com/jresearchsoftware/codex-relay/issues/97#issuecomment-6097241267) and [shared-governance #15](https://github.com/jresearchsoftware/shared-governance/issues/15).

### Native VibeVM routing — analysis accepted; bounded route C selected (2026-10-10)

[Task #99](https://github.com/jresearchsoftware/codex-relay/issues/99), Step 1 produced an [evidence-based A/B/C report and isolated routing probe](https://github.com/jresearchsoftware/codex-relay/pull/100). Exact-head [independent APPROVE](https://github.com/jresearchsoftware/codex-relay/pull/100#pullrequestreview-5478964959), Public CI PASS, squash merged at `4f0e0e38980854fcb09dc718841ade3102a8108f`. The report verified native generated file routing and stock-template customization, not actual Codex model compliance or comparative merits of WAL/spec-first. Its compatibility/disagreement matrix alone **does not decide** whether the upstream methodology would be better.

**Owner Decision:** [#99 — route C chosen](https://github.com/jresearchsoftware/codex-relay/issues/99#issuecomment-6097679412). This adopts the complete native VibeVM 1.0.7 routing generator with bounded Relay-authored core/user startup text and existing effective Relay governance. It **does not permanently reject** stock WAL, spec-first or Sync-from-Code, which are under independent comparative analysis. [Step 2 trusted Request](https://github.com/jresearchsoftware/codex-relay/issues/99#issuecomment-6097685603) admits dependency-free native routing activation; automatic dispatch was requested. No result/merge is claimed by admitting it. #99 remains open for accepted implementation and further owner choices.

### Comparative WAL/spec-first methodology assessment — separately admitted

[Task #102](https://github.com/jresearchsoftware/codex-relay/issues/102), [Step 1 Task Request](https://github.com/jresearchsoftware/codex-relay/issues/102#issuecomment-6097671313), is an owner-authorized source-only parallel investigation. Its distinct deliverable evaluates actual upstream WAL, 24-hour checkpoint handling, `Human > Spec > Tests > Code`, spec-first and Sync-from-Code against Relay's current native Issue/CR/Outcome/recovery workflow using realistic interruption, concurrency, stale-state and disagreement scenarios. Compare adoption benefits, correctness/staleness risk, and operator costs, identify measured versus unverified conclusions and explicit owner decisions. Do not change operative policy before owner disposition; the Task is open/keep-open.

### First real shared protocol migration — gated after routing and semantic audit

[Task #97](https://github.com/jresearchsoftware/codex-relay/issues/97) remains the consumer authority-transfer Task for `development-governance` / `proportional-controls`, **not** part of #99's dependency-free route or #102's methodological study. Before local duplicate removal, perform [shared-governance #15](https://github.com/jresearchsoftware/shared-governance/issues/15) cross-source semantic completeness/omission assessment, correct genuine shared-producer defects with a new independently accepted published package version if needed, and qualify the locked native consumer against the Git/native baseline. Never silently compensate missing shared semantics with leftover Relay rules. A separately admitted Task #97 Request, not this umbrella, authorizes the actual dependency adoption/atomic local transfer. Ordinary Relay behavior remains accepted until then.

### ChatGPT Project integration — accepted direction, not implemented

Owner discussion accepted a minimal Project Instructions bootstrap plus canonical GitHub/VibeVM-locked guidance, optional Project Sources cache/snapshot and reviewable generated client-specific projections; no per-message SHA/graph-re-resolution tax, no automatic live Project Settings mutation. The detailed implementation/qualification backlog is [Task #101](https://github.com/jresearchsoftware/codex-relay/issues/101), coordinated with [Relay product guidance #91](https://github.com/jresearchsoftware/codex-relay/issues/91). Project Sources availability/version inspection and any ChatGPT-specific VibeVM routing require real-client qualification.

All other potential consumer adoptions, including Documentation and Model Landscape, remain separate repository decisions. No umbrella progress/status text admits protected execution, package installation, live ChatGPT settings changes, deployment, or closure.

## PoC evidence still needed

Before an adoption decision, the umbrella should collect evidence for:

1. ownership clarity;
2. cross-repository update effort;
3. reviewability of package adoption;
4. reproducibility of exact content;
5. JIT/context-size behavior;
6. fresh-clone and offline behavior;
7. local-overlay safety;
8. absence of dual authority;
9. rollback/removal cost;
10. tooling and supply-chain cost;
11. at least one real consumer path and preferably a second independent consumer;
12. comparison with the Git/native-Skill baseline.

## Open decisions

Not yet decided:

- final public package/registry repository layout;
- whether `codex-model-landscape` itself should become public;
- whether/when a private shared-governance repository is needed;
- the exact Project Instructions synchronization model;
- whether VibeVM ultimately merits bounded adoption.

Issue closure policy: keep-open

relay91.title: Task 91 — Versioned Relay methodology and AI guidance distribution
relay91.body:
Authority model: github-native-v1

## Status

**OWNER-REQUESTED IMPLEMENTATION DIRECTION (2026-10-13); NOT YET ADMITTED.** The owner selected VibeVM-first authoring and requested development of the Relay product Skill. A qualified current-protocol execution admission is still required before allocating a Step or launching Codex. Do not change live consumer instructions/settings on charter refinement.

## Owner scope clarification — VibeVM-first authoring, optional for consumers (2026-10-13)

The owner requires **VibeVM to be part of Task #91's actual development, versioning, projection and qualification workflow**, not an optional later experiment. The accepted Relay VibeVM project/consumer from #97 is the starting point; this Task must establish and demonstrate an appropriate Relay-owned authoring/distribution path with the pinned and qualified VibeVM tooling. This is a product-guidance implementation decision, not an authorization to change Relay runtime governance, publish a shared package or deploy.

- Treat accepted **Relay product guidance** as the sole semantic authority for Relay-specific Request/Decision/CR/Outcome schemas, orchestration, identity, warning and review mechanics. Author the reusable guidance and a narrow native Codex `SKILL.md` with JIT references and human documentation; use VibeVM to assemble, version and generate or project distributable artifacts. Preserve semantic ownership of already-adopted Shared Governance principles instead of copying them into a competing canonical Relay policy.
- First qualify the actual pinned VibeVM capabilities for authoring/distributing a native Codex Skill. Use supported native VibeVM package/flow mechanisms where they fit; if a small deterministic adapter is required to emit the product Skill and no-VibeVM client artifacts, bind it to the accepted source/revision, test it and document it. Do not assume VibeVM 1.0.7 already generates the exact intended Skill or change package architecture beyond this authorization without an owner decision.
- **VibeVM is mandatory for this Task's authoring/build/maintenance qualification, but optional for external Relay consumers.** Produce version-compatible inspectable native files that a consumer can install, use, update and roll back without installing VibeVM or accessing a live registry, while preserving existing local AGENTS.md/Skills/overlays. VibeVM is not a runtime dependency of normal Codex or Relay execution.
- Align generated product guidance with the **accepted** Relay contract at its selected product revision, including any accepted #115 source changes and retained older/in-flight compatibility, but do not mistake #115's unqualified PROD deployment for installed-v4 qualification. Resolve which Shared Governance version is explicitly adopted; availability of new shared releases or protocols is not automatic consumer migration.
- Keep product guidance and its generated VibeVM/native output reviewable together in one source PR, with deterministic provenance, installation/update/rollback and fresh-clone/offline qualification. Do not require automatic registry publication, modify other repositories or live ChatGPT Project settings, or deploy product/source changes under this Task.

This clarification is part of the **pre-execution charter**. It does not independently allocate a Step, create an execution admission, bypass current protocol readiness or change the Issue closure policy.

## Problem

Relay has non-obvious product-owned methodology and operator conventions (Task Requests, Change Requests, Steps, Outcomes, naming and GitHub fields/comments, authority, admission, Writer/Reviewer separation, independent review, recovery and boundaries). A new human user or an AI agent in a consumer repository cannot infer all of this from installed binaries and GitHub Actions workflow files. VibeVM may be useful for dependency delivery, but requiring VibeVM to obtain correct Relay guidance would make the product unnecessarily dependent on an optional tool.

## Goal

Ship a minimal, coherent, **version-compatible Relay product guidance bundle** that can be installed, understood, and updated by an external consumer **without VibeVM**. Keep one product-owned semantic source for the Relay protocol and project-local overlays for each consumer; generate agent-facing adapters and human documentation from that accepted product revision where practical.

A native Codex Skill plus small `AGENTS.md` routing entry and human-readable reference documentation are the first supported path. An owner-facing repository installation/update command may integrate with the separately planned #90 interface.

## Prerequisite methodology evidence

[Relay Task #108](https://github.com/jresearchsoftware/codex-relay/issues/108) owns the **single upstream reconstruction and iterative semantic-ownership analysis**. It first reconstructs the manual-capable task-work methodology without pre-assigning rules to repositories, then separates reusable shared obligations, intentionally standardized human-facing conventions, Relay-owned technical mechanics, and client/project-local adapters. Classification may reveal gaps that require targeted deeper reconstruction within that same Task. Task #91 must not duplicate this analysis or treat current Relay syntax as automatic shared methodology.

This Task uses the independently reviewed #108 result to author and qualify the **version-compatible Relay product documentation and native Codex Skill**. [Shared Governance #14](https://github.com/jresearchsoftware/shared-governance/issues/14) separately accepts the neutral Task Handoff protocol using the same source-side evidence. Do not install or claim transfer of authority from a draft analysis; reconcile relevant shared acceptance before final compatibility validation. Relay's specific typed schemas, fields, identity-backed approvals, labels, admission, Writer/Reviewer behavior, and product release compatibility remain here.

## Required behavior

- **Product-owned contract:** Provide clear discoverable human documentation and templates/examples mapping the shared Task/Step/handoff principles where applicable to the actual Relay Task Request/Decision/Change Request/Outcome lifecycle, proper Issue/CR/PR/comment roles, naming, submission/admission, completion, review, warning handling and operator boundaries. Identify which rules are core Relay protocol versus optional project-specific approval/merge policy. Do not turn consumer-dependent choices into universal Relay requirements.
- **Native AI adapter:** Supply a focused `SKILL.md` and on-demand references for supported Codex clients, with a minimal repository bootstrap/routing instruction rather than loading the entire methodology into every agent prompt. State supported agent/client discovery and paths explicitly; do not assume a Skill installed in a Git repository automatically updates ChatGPT Project Instructions.
- **Human usability:** An ordinary user can find the protocol and practical authoring examples without understanding Skill loading or having an AI client. Show at least a normal task, a Change Request/remediation, an Outcome and an independent review/continuation boundary.
- **Distribution and maintenance:** Deliver guidance as a deterministic, inspectable integration artifact from a selected accepted Relay product version, alongside but not inseparably coupled to managed workflows. Provide a bounded initial install and explicit update/reconciliation path with provenance and an intelligible diff. No mandatory VibeVM installation, moving-latest runtime lookup, network fetch during ordinary execution, or private registry.
- **Local ownership:** Preserve user-authored `AGENTS.md`, existing Skills and other project-local conventions; use a small owned block or explicit proposal, not wholesale overwrite. Detect collisions, managed drift and changes that could create competing instruction authority. Owners review and publish resulting repository changes through their normal process.
- **Layering:** Relay-specific Task Request/Decision/Change Request/Outcome schemas and actor/execution/approval mechanics remain canonical in Relay and travel with its revision. Once separately accepted and adopted, portable Task/Step/handoff principles are owned by Shared Governance; until then, preserve existing accepted consumer/Relay rules. Optional neutral cross-project governance and VibeVM packages remain independent per #59. Live Issue/CR/PR evidence, current Step/profile/head/checks, and owner decisions are never packaged as static guidance.
- **ChatGPT Project:** Where useful, offer an optional concise, ready-to-apply Project Instructions/bootstrap artifact with explicit provenance and manual owner review/application if no qualified settings interface exists. This is separate from native repository Skill projection and must not be represented as automatic ChatGPT project synchronization.
- **Compatibility:** Guidance should describe the behavior of the actual selected Relay/workflow contract; updating a consumer must not silently introduce incompatible process rules. Preserve a straightforward rollback/removal path for generated guidance without deleting local content.

## Relationship to existing Tasks

- #108 owns prerequisite reconstruction and semantic partition; shared-governance #14 owns the neutral protocol. This Task owns the Relay product guidance/Skill, not either upstream analysis or shared acceptance.
- #90 owns the general repository onboarding/status/update UX and managed workflow integration; this Task owns the guidance contents, supported agent projection and distribution behavior. They may share one future consumer-facing command without duplicating implementations.
- #63 owns one-shot host installation/update and its repository integration output. Guidance may accompany the versioned output without broadening #63's host lifecycle.
- #59 and #83 cover optional VibeVM/shared cross-project governance and comparison with Git/native-Skill delivery. This Task is **Relay product-contract distribution**, not a shared-governance extraction or a VibeVM adoption decision.
- #84/#85/#86 own the underlying multi-repository behavior and configuration, not the authored guidance.

## Boundaries

Do not modify Relay runtime authority, native approval/merge/closure rules, Writer/Reviewer trust separation, GitHub repository settings, host deployment, credentials or external AI client settings. No mandatory VibeVM **for consumers**, new mandatory package registry, universal policy engine, automatic agent-settings overwrite, or duplicated independently maintained methodology.

## Starting state and authority

Target source repository: `jresearchsoftware/codex-relay`. Resolve current accepted `AGENTS.md`, product/task contracts, deployment workflow interface, and the relevant #59/#63/#90 boundaries at future admission. No Step, route, PR, SHA, or profile is assigned merely by creating this Issue.

## Issue lifecycle

Issue closure policy: keep-open

Guidance authoring, native consumer projection, independent review and representative fresh-user/agent qualification are not yet performed. Keep open until a full supported consumer installation and update/rollback path is independently accepted, with any unresolved client-specific limitations explicitly disposed.

## Recommended model budget

- Recommended Codex model: `gpt-6.1-sol`.
- Recommended Codex effort: `xhigh`.
- Reason: protocol consistency, generation/projection ownership, client-specific loading and safe compatibility/overlay behavior require careful cross-contract review.
- Escalation conditions: a proposed change to product authority semantics, consumer control boundaries or external client settings requires an owner decision before execution.
- De-escalation conditions: a separately bounded documentation-only subtask may use a cheaper owner-resolved profile.

## Validation

- Verify VibeVM-first source authoring and generated native Codex Skill/projections with the pinned supported VibeVM tool; prove generated outputs are version-bound, inspectable and reproducible, with explicit limitations of the tool rather than asserted support.

- Clean supported consumer can obtain and use complete human-readable guidance and native Codex Skill from the exact selected Relay revision, with **no VibeVM binary, cache, registry or network at execution time** after artifacts are committed.
- Native Skill discovery/routing, JIT reference loading and links work from a fresh clone in the supported Codex environment.
- Examples match accepted Relay schemas, templates, workflow contracts and current published protocol; review finds no parallel authority or contradictory process requirements.
- Existing user `AGENTS.md`/Skills and local overlays survive fresh projection, update, rollback and removal; collisions/drift get a reviewable result instead of silent replacement.
- Version change produces an understandable bounded diff and does not silently switch a consumer to moving policy.
- Human-only flow is usable without AI; any ChatGPT Project Instructions path is truthfully qualified as manual or supported automation.
- Run task-specific tests and applicable full candidate checks from `AGENTS.md`. Complete independent exact-head review remains mandatory.

## Completion

Publish one canonical Codex Outcome with exact candidate head, evidence, limitations and warnings; stop for independent exact-head review and separately governed acceptance. Backlog creation does not authorize implementation, deployment, changes to live AI client settings, or Issue closure.

shared30.title: Define cross-project onboarding and governance adoption workflow
shared30.body:
## Status and authority

**BACKLOG / DESIGN OPEN — NOT ADMITTED FOR EXECUTION.** This Task records a future reusable **project onboarding/adoption procedure**. Creating it does not allocate a Step, launch Codex, edit a repository, activate a governance topic, change GitHub settings, update consumers, publish a package, or authorize merge/closure. Implementation requires a later explicit owner Decision under the then-accepted Task Handoff protocol.

## Background / why this is separate

[Task #13](https://github.com/jresearchsoftware/shared-governance/issues/13) delivered the workflow-aware GitHub repository governance topic in Development Governance **2.1.0**. That passive topic offers PR-driven development, owner-authorized direct-`main` evidence maintenance, publication and mixed paths, with proportional setup recommendations, a short checklist and event-driven configuration verification.

**Installing or updating the VibeVM package activates nothing and performs no audit or GitHub mutation.** An owner can deliberately ask an agent to identify the project's workflow, select a profile and inspect actual settings. The owner agreed this is sufficient for #13, and that a **separate future project-onboarding procedure** may be more prescriptive *when onboarding is intentionally initiated*. Do not retrofit an implicit always-on trigger into #13.

[Task #15](https://github.com/jresearchsoftware/shared-governance/issues/15) requires semantic completeness during shared extraction and consumer adoption: removing a local canonical duplicate must not mask omitted reusable obligations. [Task #17](https://github.com/jresearchsoftware/shared-governance/issues/17) keeps the single-package architecture until actual selective-adoption demand justifies revisiting it.

**Different ownership boundary:** [Codex Relay #90](https://github.com/jresearchsoftware/codex-relay/issues/90) owns *Relay product* repository workflow/manifest projection, installation, status/update and Reviewer-only support; [Relay #91](https://github.com/jresearchsoftware/codex-relay/issues/91) owns Relay-specific AI guidance and Skills. This Task owns **cross-project Development Governance onboarding**, not Relay provisioning or its client distribution.

## Goal

Define a **small, human-initiated, manual-capable and reusable onboarding procedure** for a new or existing project that wants to assess or adopt the Development Governance package/topics. It should connect the project's current accepted authority, available shared protocols, real workflows and actual GitHub configuration into an actionable recommendation and, only after separate authorization, a reviewable adoption/change. It must be useful without Codex Relay, new services or a machine-readable repository-type registry.

Distinguish at least:
1. **Package availability / installation**: the VibeVM package and pinned/materialized files may exist without any new normative topic being adopted.
2. **Explicit topic/policy adoption**: the project selects which guidance to accept, identifies applicable project-owned rules, reconciles duplicates and exceptions, and records an owner decision through existing durable authority.
3. **Repository configuration**: changing actual GitHub rulesets, merge settings, credentials, checks or deployment/publication tooling is a separate protected action, never a side effect of package install or policy adoption.

## Candidate onboarding flow to evaluate

1. **Discover before prescribing.** Read existing project instructions, applicable Decisions and source/history as needed; observe current human/bot workflows, protected refs, release paths, validations, manual versus Relay operation and existing dependency/boot projection. For a new project with no settled profile, offer reasonable choices rather than inventing a binding classification.
2. **Choose the scope of adoption.** Identify suitable Development Governance topics and their relevance, consumer-local overlays, explicit exceptions, package identity/version pinning and loading route. Use Task #15's source-to-shared obligation mapping when migrating existing canonical rules: no silent omission, dual authority or gap while replacing duplicates. Do not require every topic.
3. **Select workflows with the owner.** Apply #13's conditional PR, routine direct-`main`, generated-publication and hybrid guidance per change path. Record only the durable choices needed to make future decisions; do not invent a mandatory `repository.type` field, universal PR gate or Relay dependency.
4. **Read-only configuration/evidence assessment.** Compare the chosen profile to actual GitHub merge options, effective branch/tag protections and rulesets (including inheritance, bypass and enforcement state), appropriate check/reviewer identities and publication writers, as authorized/available. Distinguish VERIFIED, GAP, NOT APPLICABLE and UNVERIFIED; do not treat inaccessible/404 evidence as proof of absence. Apply proportional-controls to mismatches and viable alternatives. Reuse existing onboarding evidence when fresh.
5. **Decision and separately authorized action.** Present a concise proposed adoption/configuration delta, risk/operator cost and exceptions. The owner can accept, change or decline it. Any repository files, VibeVM dependency/lock/boot change, setting change, credential or workflow action follows the receiving project's own admission/review/permission rules; read back actual results rather than reporting proposed settings as enforced.
6. **Handoff/maintenance.** Retain a lightweight outcome in existing Issue/PR/onboarding records. Recheck affected setup when material local policy, workflows, identities, permissions, settings or observed drift change; no per-session, per-Task or mandatory calendar settings audit.

## Design questions (not pre-decided requirements)

- Is a concise shared conditional protocol warranted, or do a small reusable operator checklist plus existing #13/#15 guidance suffice? Avoid duplicating their normative content.
- What minimal existing-project evidence/owner disposition makes onboarding **complete** versus **deferred/unverified**? What is the cheapest human-friendly entrypoint (e.g., an ordinary task to "onboard this project")?
- Which steps should be required *once onboarding is intentionally invoked*, while keeping dependency installation and mere availability completely passive?
- How should a project choose **not to adopt** some topics, or defer settings changes, without importing silent authority or proliferating metadata/templates?

## Acceptance examples

1. New manual-only PR development repository: suggest a profile, owner selects it, check meaningful GitHub configuration without demanding Relay or a second reviewer identity.
2. Living evidence/reference repository: retain explicitly authorized routine direct-`main` updates; distinguish material recommendation changes; do not enable `Restrict updates` or PR-only protection by accident.
3. Existing mixed source/publication repository: preserve normal PR review and independent generated-release path; qualify retained branches, tag immutability and supported writer/bypass scope without blanket exceptions.
4. Existing consumer with local duplicated governance: preserve complete reusable semantics and accepted local exceptions, demonstrate explicit migration of ownership/boot/dependency without relying on leftover duplicates.
5. Missing GitHub admin access, plan or opaque API: report an honest evidence gap and proportionate owner choices, not a fabricated PASS or automatic privilege escalation.
6. Mere VibeVM install/update without explicit onboarding/adoption: no changed normative requirements, no settings audit, no consumer configuration mutation.

## Deliverables and boundaries

- A short, source-grounded decision on the appropriate reusable form (protocol or documented procedure), preserving Task #13/#15 semantics and product-owned boundaries.
- When subsequently admitted, the smallest coherent guidance/checklist plus proportionate realistic walks; if the package is changed, an honestly classified new whole-package version, normal source/export/self-adoption qualification, independent review and separately authorized release.
- No new daemon, settings synchronizer, mandatory global registry, periodic audit, implicit activation on package update, universal PR mandate, Relay workflow projection, live repository mutation or consumer migration under this backlog Issue.

**Issue lifecycle: KEEP OPEN / BACKLOG** until explicitly admitted and the accepted onboarding-procedure deliverable and its adoption boundary are resolved.

shared15.title: Preserve semantic completeness in shared-governance extraction and adoption
shared15.body:
## Owner decision (2026-10-10)

**ACCEPTED PRINCIPLE — preserve semantic completeness across governance extraction and consumer migration.** This is a reusable governance rule, not merely a textual deduplication convention. The owner identified repeated omissions when moving project instructions and development rules between projects, including historical Documentation/Codex Relay separation and the new shared `proportional-controls` package.

A consumer appearing to work because its leftover local instructions compensate for missing shared rules is **not** proof of successful extraction. A migration must not silently turn a missing reusable requirement into a consumer-local overlay.

## Goal

Make cross-project governance extraction, package adaptation and later consumer adoption preserve the complete **accepted reusable semantics**: obligations, applicability, qualifiers, exceptions, protected boundaries, expected agent routing and user/operator behaviors. Promote this minimal invariant into the accepted reusable authoring/migration procedure in this repository, so future protocol extractions use it without rediscovering losses after adoption.

## Required acceptance principle

1. **Establish a semantic baseline before moving ownership.** Read all relevant current canonical policy slices and, where needed to account for earlier splits/adaptations, their accepted source history, old original instructions, relevant project integrations and outcome/correction history. Do not presume one current paragraph or one like-named file contains the complete domain contract. Limit archaeology to decisions/behaviors relevant to the domain, not unbounded repo history.
2. **Map obligations, not strings.** Account for each material reusable guarantee, trigger, exemption, cost/authority boundary, operator flow and routing condition in a reviewable source-to-shared coverage record. Distinguish exact preservation, meaning-preserving reformulation, intentional accepted semantic change, omission/weakening, and genuinely consumer-specific binding.
3. **Classify missing behavior by ownership.** Shared/cross-project semantics omitted or weakened in the producer are **producer migration defects**, not something to leave silently in the original consumer. Fix them in canonical shared source and independently accept a new package version before relying on the shared package. A product-owned contract or deliberate local overlay stays local only with explicit, defensible ownership rationale. Do not change or republish the frozen `development-governance@0.1.0` artifact/tag to repair omissions.
4. **Exercise both perspectives.** Verify shared guidance can support at least one other plausible consumer or scenario without help from the old project's local residual rules, and verify the original consumer after replacing its reusable duplicates. Prove correct loading/application where possible; separate file/text evidence, CLI behavior and actual model behavior, and mark unsupported claims as evidence gaps. A scenario is evidence, not a new always-on global testing gate.
5. **Transfer authority atomically.** On each consumer's separately admitted migration, adopt pinned reviewed shared content, remove the genuinely duplicated canonical local guidance, preserve documented product-specific bindings and verified local overlays, and check no rule becomes missing, silently weaker or doubly authoritative. Prefer clean Git rollback and normal independent exact-head review.
6. **Scale the evidence.** The required result is a concise, reviewable semantic coverage argument; do not introduce a standing ledger, rigid global checklist, new service, mandatory extra owner step or exhaustive manual line mapping for trivial editorial changes. Apply proportional controls for any proposed new gate. Record material omissions and owner decisions in existing Task/PR/review evidence.

## Scope of source implementation

- Update the smallest correct accepted source-governance layer, likely `AGENTS.md` and a concise existing authoring/consumer document if the detail cannot fit there, to establish this invariant for **future** shared protocol extractions and migrations.
- Treat `proportional-controls` as the first demonstration: compare the frozen public ordinary flow protocol with its Relay-local provenance, record any already-obvious candidate omissions and their classification, and explicitly pass unresolved findings to the consumer Task. This issue alone does not authorize rewriting or publishing a new package.
- Link consumer acceptance to [Relay Task #97](https://github.com/jresearchsoftware/codex-relay/issues/97), while keeping the separate [native boot/routing investigation #99](https://github.com/jresearchsoftware/codex-relay/issues/99) independent.
- Qualify relevant documentation/procedure checks and capture warning disposition. Any implementation belongs in a normal source-owned branch and PR with independent exact-head review; this Issue is the authority location for the shared reusable rule.

## Boundaries

No edits to other repositories, no automatic consumer migration or duplicate removal, no changed published `v0.1.0` tag/source bytes, no new remote release, package registry/permission/credential changes, no deployment/host mutation, no new enforcement gate or material user/operator change absent owner authorization. Preserve canonical Task/PR/Reviewer authority and the distinction between shared rules and project-owned product contracts.

The existing no-multi-repository-Writer boundary means source implementation, if/when admitted, is a separate manual-Codex or otherwise explicitly authorized reviewable PR. **Creating this Issue neither allocates a Step nor launches work.**

## Completion and lifecycle

Issue closure policy: keep-open

Keep open until the reusable rule is accepted into source governance and an initial concrete coverage assessment or documented follow-up is recorded. No automatic successor Task/Step, release, merge or Issue closure is authorized by this charter.

## Current execution admission — Step 1 (2026-10-10)

**OWNER-AUTHORIZED MANUAL CODEX EXECUTION.** The owner has now authorized this first implementation/review-candidate attempt and confirmed the execution profile. The earlier statement that merely creating this Issue did not admit work remains true; the present authorization is separate and applies only to this Step.

- Repository: `jresearchsoftware/shared-governance`.
- Task/Step: `Task 15 — Step 1 — Preserve semantic completeness in shared-governance extraction and adoption`.
- Required starting branch/head: `main` at `3fa243b83a630ccd4973114e5cad12e1351d1558`. Normalize to this exact starting head; stop and report on an unreconcilable mismatch or unrelated local work.
- Route: **owner-launched manual Codex** in a dedicated local thread, not automatic Relay/Writer.
- Codex model: `gpt-6.1-sol`.
- Reasoning effort: `xhigh`.
- Subagents: **On**, for independent semantic/source comparisons when useful.
- Execute the already-defined scope and boundaries in this Issue. Use ordinary non-force source branch/commit/PR, complete relevant checks, and publish a concise English exact-head Outcome on this canonical Issue. Preserve discovered material omissions and warning limitations in the review evidence; do not claim the frozen public `v0.1.0` changed or initiate a consumer migration.
- Finish at the independent exact-head review boundary; no self-approval, merge, release, later Step, or Issue closure is admitted. Current closure policy remains `keep-open`.
